# Goethe — Selected Poems: Permanence in Change (Nims, 1983)

[Source index](../../../README.md) · [Reading entrance](../../../../../../README.md) · [48 movements](../../../../../../section-rooms/README.md)

## Chicago 18 forms

**Full note (selected edition; collation Open):** Johann Wolfgang von Goethe, “Permanence in Change,” trans. John Frederick Nims, in *Selected Poems*, ed. Christopher Middleton, vol. 1 of *Goethe: The Collected Works* (Princeton, NJ: Princeton University Press, 1983), 169.

**Shortened note:** Goethe, “Permanence in Change,” 169.

**Bibliography:** Goethe, Johann Wolfgang von. *Selected Poems*. Edited by Christopher Middleton. Vol. 1 of *Goethe: The Collected Works*. Princeton, NJ: Princeton University Press, 1983. Translation of “Dauer im Wechsel” by John Frederick Nims.

These forms identify the selected object. They do not certify inspection of its page 169. The German-facing p 168 remains an acquisition locator. The 1994 reprint and 1970 magazine publication are different witnesses.

## Essay use and whole-poem recovery

This house supplies the literary witness for the already admitted `mytheme-goethe-permanence-change`, destined for `submission-package/essay/symbolon/mytheme/worlds/german-literature/goethe-permanence-change/WHOLE.md`. Its ratified alias “Permanence and Change” names the same poem; the source uses the edition's “in.” The whole is a poetic refraction of A11/A12's Two Ones and A36's return, not a formal proof of QL or an equation attributed to Goethe.

The full German poem moves from blossom lost to wind, through ripening and a changing river, to changed perception, aging limbs and the passing bearer of a name. Its last movement gathers beginning and end while distinguishing the heart's content from the spirit's form. The native Mytheme must retain this embodied temporal loss and artistic return; a timeless abstraction would not carry the complete poem.

The final-stanza fragment named in the harmonised quilt belongs here. No independently distinguishable Taylor utterance quoting it was recovered; ratification licenses its programme use, not an attribution of Nims's wording to Taylor. Selige Sehnsucht, Eins und Alles and Faust remain distinct works.

## Material metadata and access provenance

- **Selected object:** Nims's translation in Middleton's 1983 collection. No local full copy found in the inspected repository/intake or Apple Books title metadata.
- **Primary publication metadata:** [Poetry Foundation, August 1970](https://www.poetryfoundation.org/poetrymagazine/issue/71009/august-1970), volume 116; historical index identifies p 345. [Digitized entry](https://www.poetryfoundation.org/poetrymagazine/poems/31637/song-of-the-traveller-at-evening) names poem and translator; shared browse redirect and 403 image prevented page collation.
- **Selected-edition locator:** [Segall, Goethe and Whitehead, footnote 117](https://footnotes2plato.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/08/goethe-and-whitehead-steps-to-a-science-of-organism-final.pdf) identifies 1983 p 169. This secondary lead is not primary quotation verification.
- **Reprint locator:** [Google Books, 1994 Selected Poems](https://books.google.com/books/about/Selected_Poems.html?hl=en&id=LGDW6Df_y_gC&output=html_text) lists Nims at 169; no silent promotion to 1983 collation.
- **German whole witness:** [Klett publisher's 2010 teaching excerpt](https://www2.klett.de/sixcms/media.php/229/350470_0239_Goethe_Dauer.pdf), one page, all 40 lines, explicitly sourced to Goethe, *Sämtliche Werke. Briefe, Tagebücher und Gespräche*, I.2, *Gedichte 1800–1832* (Deutscher Klassiker Verlag, 1988), 78–79. All 40 lines read via extracted text on 2026-09-06; image fetch 403. This is a separately identified German witness within the selected translation's verification trail, not Nims's wording.
- **Identity crosscheck:** [Goethes Lyrik digital, 93052](https://goethe-lyrik.net/wissen/93052/) confirms title/incipit and WA I.1: 119. It does not establish Nims's exact translation.
- **Authorial NOTES:** absent at admission; none created. Full modern translation is neither copied nor stored here.

> Double aspects of the One

- **Locator:** selected 1983 edition, p 169, final stanza; quoted fragment independently located in Segall's quotation, footnote 117.
- **Status:** Open — selected-edition quotation not collated.
- **Verification:** exact six-word retrieval lead checked 2026-09-06; no claim of primary print transcription.
- **Source relation:** resonant with the native Two Ones; excerpt lead only for Nims wording.
- **Evidential action:** identifies the fragment and blocks a second-poem substitution.
- **Consumers:** `mytheme-goethe-permanence-change`; A11; A12; A36.

## Passage card — `goethe-1983-selected-poems-nims-q002` — German content and form
^goethe-1983-selected-poems-nims-q002

> Den Gehalt in deinem Busen / Und die Form in deinem Geist.

- **Locator:** Dauer im Wechsel, lines 39–40; Klett 2010 single-page excerpt from FA I.2: 78–79. Slash denotes the printed line break.
- **Status:** German digital-witness wording-verified; selected 1983 translation quotation remains Open.
- **Verification:** transcribed from the complete line-numbered Klett extracted text 2026-09-06; not image-collated and not checked in the 1988 printed volume.
- **Source relation:** extracted from the explicitly named German witness; resonant with the essay's whole-bearing return.
- **Evidential action:** supports the actual closing distinction; qualifies a flattened static-One reading.
- **Consumers:** `mytheme-goethe-permanence-change`; A12; A36.
- **Use boundary:** this German wording does not authorize an invented Nims English translation. Native QL standing survives the translation debt.
